newsitem.title: UK: Precious metals weaker, led by sickly silver.
newsitem.headline: Precious metals weaker, led by sickly silver.

text.p: The precious metals slid to fresh lows on Friday, following a plunge in silver below the key $5 level as disillusioned investors pulled out of the market.
"It broke through an important trend line going back three years last night and that's knocked the confidence out of the market quite a lot," a dealer said.
Silver closed in London at $4.87 an ounce, a 14-cent drop from the previous finish.
A sell-off orginating on New York's futures market on Thursday picked up steam again on Friday afternoon after silver fixed at an 18-month low of $4.9450.
Further drops to as low as $4.60 an ounce could not be ruled out, some analysts said.
Gold also weakened, but managed to escape the wholesale damage wreaked on silver. It closed $1.10 lower at $381.75 an ounce after fixing at $381.75, the lowest since July 9, 1996.
Analysts said the key support for gold was $380.00, which would be followed by $378.00.
Palladium also felt the crunch. Its close was little changed from Thursday's lower levels, but it fixed at a fresh three-year low of $119.50 an ounce, beneath the key $120 level.
Platinum, which ended $1.70 lower at $387.00 an ounce, also hit recent lows. Its fixing at $387.25 matched this year's July 4 low, which was the lowest fixing since April 20, 1994.

Investor interest has been scarce in the platinum group metals recently demonstrated by platinum's inability to get back over $400.00 and the gradual erosion of palladium prices to around $120.00 from around $131.00 at the end of July.

"Part of the trouble is nobody knows when the Russians will start selling again and that puts investors off and discourages consumers from carrying stocks," one dealer said. Russia is a major producer of platinum and palladium.
The sharp drop in silver proved the market's vulnerability after days of hovering just above $5.00, analysts said.
"There could be some more to go on silver which isn't too oversold yet. I'd stay short till it was back over $4.95," one dealer said.
Volumes were higher on Friday than had been seen in recent nervous sessions, dealers said.
"Funds like selling into weakness and there may be more weakness to come yet," a dealer said. "But the psychology is that if everyone thinks it's going one way, it won't."
